user_query: I am a YouTuber. Last night, someone bypassed my two-factor authentication, took over my entire YouTube channel, changed the password, and is livestreaming crypto scams to my 1 million subscribers!
legal_text_raw: If any person without permission... provides any assistance to any person to facilitate access to a computer... or charges the services availed of by a person to the account of another person by tampering with or manipulating any computer... he shall be liable...
layman_explanation: Your account has been hijacked. Do not engage with the hacker. Immediately tweet to @TeamYouTube with an alternate account, freeze linked bank/AdSense accounts, and file an FIR with the Cyber Cell under IT Act 66 for 'Computer Related Offences / Hacking'.

user_query: The builder promised me a flat with a 500 sq ft carpet area in the brochure and agreement. Now during handover, I measured it and it's barely 400 sq ft. He says 'super built-up area' covers the rest.
legal_text_raw: A promoter shall... make available to the allottee the sanctioned plans, layout plans... carpet area... 'carpet area' means the net usable floor area of an apartment, excluding the area covered by the external walls, areas under services shafts, exclusive balcony... but includes the area covered by the internal partition walls of the apartment.
layman_explanation: Under RERA, properties can ONLY be sold based on the 'Net Carpet Area'. Selling based on ambiguous 'super built-up area' to hide a smaller flat is an illegal, deceptive practice. File a complaint with your State RERA Authority; the builder must refund the proportional money for the missing 100 sq ft.

user_query: An agent promised to get me a work visa for Dubai. I transferred him 3 Lakhs, he gave me a printed visa paper at the airport. At immigration, the officers told me the visa was printed on a home printer and is completely fake. The agent's phone is switched off.
legal_text_raw: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person... or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything... shall be punished with imprisonment... which may extend to seven years...
layman_explanation: This is a classic 'Visa Fraud/Cheating' scheme (previously IPC 420, now under BNS 316). He has committed cheating and forgery. Keep the bank transfer receipts, WhatsApp chats, and the fake visa copy safe. Immediately lodge an FIR for criminal breach of trust and cheating with the police.

user_query: My neighbor has started aggressive digging right next to the common wall separating our houses to build a basement. My wall has developed massive cracks and might collapse onto my family while we sleep. The police say it's a civil property issue and won't intervene.
legal_text_raw: Whenever an Executive Magistrate... receives information that any building, or tent or structure, or any tree is in such a condition that it is likely to fall and thereby cause injury to persons living or carrying on business in the neighbourhood... he may make a conditional order requiring the person... to remove, repair or support it...
layman_explanation: If the police claim it's merely a civil dispute, they are ignoring the imminent danger to life. You can urgently approach the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) or Executive Magistrate under Section 152 of the BNSS regarding a 'public nuisance / dangerous structure'. The SDM can immediately issue orders to halt the digging.

user_query: My friend borrowed 5 Lakhs from me in cash two years ago. Yesterday he finally gave me a cheque, but when I deposited it, it 'bounced' because of 'Insufficient Funds'. He is now laughing at me saying I can't do anything about a friendly loan.
legal_text_raw: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person... is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient... such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence...
layman_explanation: Your friend is wrong. A bounced cheque for discharging a debt is a criminal offense under the Negotiable Instruments Act. You MUST send a formal legal notice to him within 30 days of receiving the bank memo. If he fails to pay within 15 days of the notice, file a criminal case in court.

source_act: Section 125, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (formerly CrPC 125)
user_query: My husband threw me out of his house. I am a housewife with zero income. He earns 2 Lakhs a month but claims in family court that he 'resigned' and has no job just to avoid paying me maintenance.
legal_text_raw: If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain... his wife, unable to maintain herself... a Magistrate of the first class may, upon proof of such neglect or refusal, order such person to make a monthly allowance for the maintenance of his wife...
layman_explanation: Indian courts are strictly against this tactic. A husband's 'voluntary resignation' does not absolve him of his duty to maintain his wife. The court will look at his 'earning capacity', qualifications, and past salary, not just his current zero-income claim. File for interim maintenance under Section 125 BNSS immediately.

source_act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
user_query: I just found out my husband has been secretly cheating on me with his colleague for 2 years. I confronted him, and now he is threatening to throw me out of the flat. The flat is registered solely in his name.
legal_text_raw: Every woman in a domestic relationship shall have the right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has any right, title or beneficial interest in the same... The aggrieved person shall not be evicted or excluded from the shared household or any part of it by the respondent save in accordance with the procedure established by law.
layman_explanation: He cannot throw you out. Even if the flat is 100% owned by him, because you lived there after marriage, it is legally your 'Shared Household'. You must urgently file an application under the Domestic Violence Act to get a 'Residence Order' preventing him from evicting you.

user_query: I got married exactly 3 months ago. It was an arranged marriage, and I've discovered my wife is violently aggressive and lied about having severe schizophrenia. Our lives are a nightmare. The lawyer says I have to wait 1 year to file for divorce!
legal_text_raw: It shall not be competent for any court to entertain any petition for dissolution of a marriage... unless at the date of the presentation of the petition one year has elapsed since the date of the marriage: Provided that the court may... allow a petition to be presented... on the ground that the case is one of exceptional hardship to the petitioner...
layman_explanation: While the general rule is a 1-year wait, there is a specific exception. Because she hid a severe mental illness and is violent, your lawyer can file an application to waive the 1-year ban citing 'Exceptional Hardship'. Gather medical proof and file immediately.

source_act: Section 28, Indian Contract Act, 1872 & Non-Compete Jurisprudence
user_query: I worked as a lead developer at an ed-tech startup. I just quit to start my own rival ed-tech company. My old boss sent a legal notice saying my employment contract had a '2-year Non-Compete Clause' banning me from starting any competing business in India.
legal_text_raw: Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. (Exception: Sale of Goodwill).
layman_explanation: Do not panic. In India, Post-Employment Non-Compete clauses are completely null and void under Section 27 of the Contract Act. The moment you resign, your employer cannot legally stop you from starting a rival business or joining a competitor. His legal notice is meant to scare you, it is largely unenforceable.

user_query: My co-founder and I started a Pvt Ltd company with a 50-50 equity split. We didn't sign a founders' agreement. Now he has stopped working, refuses to talk to me, and won't resign. He still owns 50% of the company!
legal_text_raw: In the absence of a Founders' Agreement or specific Articles of Association (AoA) detailing 'vesting schedules' or 'deadlock resolution', the removal of a director/shareholder requires adherence to the Companies Act, which is difficult without majority voting power.
layman_explanation: This is a 'Founder Deadlock'. Because you didn't have a vesting schedule, you cannot automatically take back his shares, and at 50-50, you cannot vote him out of the company. You must immediately hire a corporate lawyer to attempt a buyout negotiation, or file for oppression/mismanagement in the NCLT to force a split.
